chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:

We performed hajj while we were doing it for the first time, and we performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah fourteen circuits. So we asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about that, and he said: There is no problem; seven are for you, and seven are discarded.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Ṣafā, one of the two points of saʿy.
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah, the other point of saʿy.
key_terms.تُطْرَحُ: It is set aside or disregarded.
key_terms.شَوْطًا: A circuit or lap in the ritual movement.
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: A person performing hajj for the first time, having not performed it before.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem or harm in this case.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs fourteen circuits of saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who performs more than seven circuits in the saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah during hajj. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the valid seven count for the pilgrim, while the extra seven are disregarded.
